Congressman Gomez is the Founder and Chair of the Congressional Dads Caucus and Congressional Renters Caucus. He is a member of the Congressional Hispanic Caucus (CHC), Congressional Asian Pacific American Caucus (CAPAC), and Future Forum. Affordability | U.S. Representative Jimmy Gomez Working families have been stretched thin over the years, with some working two or more jobs to get by. This economy isn't working for ordinary Americans.&nbsp; Nearly 59% of families do not have enough savings to cover a $1,000 emergency expense. Just 4 out of 10 student loan borrowers are current on their loans, with 35% of borrowers 60 days delinquent or longer. Families are spending more on groceries than they have in over three decades. Child care and rent are skyrocketing, and home ownership costs are growing out of reach.&nbsp;</p> <p>Congress must prioritize solving the issues that make a difference for working and middle-class families, like affordable housing, child support, and healthcare. Focusing on these issues establishes the foundation for a fairer economy and develops the opportunity for every family to get ahead.&nbsp;</p> <p><b>Housing: </b></p> <p>The American Dream of owning a home feels further out of reach than ever before. That is why I authored the Affordable Homeownership Opportunity Act, which would give first-time homebuyers between $25,000 and $50,000 towards a downpayment and help incentivize developers to build more starter homes instead of unaffordable McMansions.&nbsp;</p> <p>We also need to address the skyrocketing rents across Los Angeles. That's why I am working to pass legislation to increase federal rental assistance, expand the supply of affordable housing, and remove barriers that prevent people from finding and keeping affordable homes.&nbsp;</p> <p><b>Raising a Family:</b></p> <p>No family should be overburdened by the cost of child care. That's why I introduced the Child Care Infrastructure Act and the Child Care Workforce Development Act, two bills that address America's child care crisis with robust investment in early learning facilities and early educators. The bills would build more classrooms, hire more teachers, and decrease costs for providers and parents. Affordable child care helps working parents keep their kids safe while they go to work to provide for their families.&nbsp;&

Children and Families | U.S. Representative Jimmy Gomez As a father of a toddler who represents the working families of Los Angeles in Congress, I know firsthand how challenging it has been for families to thrive. Costs are going up, and parents are working twice as hard just to keep up. Worse, child care costs continue to skyrocket and it’s harder than ever to find access to high-quality child care. It is unacceptable that the average parent spends over 20% of their income on child care.<br /> <b>That’s why I founded the first-ever Congressional Dads Caucus, a group of Member of Congress – moms and dads – dedicated to using our platform as parents and elected officials to uplift the voices of working families and champion policies that help kids succeed.</b><b> <br /> </b> <br /> With costs continuing to rise on everything from housing to groceries, I’m fighting to significantly increase the Child Tax Credit and make sure it’s paid monthly. <b>Families can’t wait until April for their tax credit—they need help now to meet their basic needs like child care, healthcare, and housing expenses.</b><b> <br /> </b><br /> The United States is one of the only developed countries without a national paid leave program, and just 27% of Americans in the private sector have access to paid leave<b>. I am committed to ensuring a permanent, equitable, and comprehensive national paid family and medical leave program that serves all families</b>. Small Business and Entrepreneurship | U.S. Representative Jimmy Gomez Los Angeles is driven by small businesses and entrepreneurs, from street food vendors to content creators. Our community in Los Angeles, in particular, serves as a global hub for entertainment due to its deep roots in media and rich history as home to a thriving, diverse community of creative talent.&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;</p> <p>Small businesses face unique challenges, and as your Representative, I'm committed to leveraging federal resources to help our businesses and community grow.&nbsp;</p> <p>I am strong advocate for <b>increasing federal appropriations to the Community Development Financial Institution (CDFI) Fund</b>, which provides lenders with affordable credit and capital for small businesses in our community. In addition<b>, I'll defend the Minority Business Development Agency</b>, which helps new entrepreneurs develop their business knowhow so that they can succeed and get ahead.&nbsp;</p> <p>The emerging creator economy is a rising industry driven by digital entrepreneurs who actively shape culture and influence public opinion and consumer trends across key sectors such as tourism, fashion, lifestyle, fitness, and technology. As independent business owners, they face many of the same challenges as traditional small businesses, along with hurdles unique to the content creation industry. That is why <b>I wrote to the Small Business Administration (SBA) to urge them support this fast-growing industry by providing services and programs that will help content creator small businesses continue to thrive and contribute to our economy.</b>&nbsp;</p> <p>Whether it is casework assistance with the SBA or helping maintain a strong workforce to help meet the needs of small businesses through the Federal Job Corps, I'll never stop fighting to ensure our community has the resources needed for our local economy to grow.</p>" /> Skip to Content Small Business and Entrepreneurship Share on Facebook Share on Twitter Print this Page Share by Email Los Angeles is driven by small businesses and entrepreneurs, from street food v

Social Security and Medicare | U.S. Representative Jimmy Gomez <p><b>Social Security provides financial security to those in retirement, living with a disability, or grieving a loved one.</b> This invaluable program delivers critical benefits to over 90,000 recipients in our district, and keeps 22.5 million Americans across the country out of poverty. I will always fight to protect Social Security--no matter who holds office.&nbsp;&nbsp;</p> <p><b>Programs like Medicare and Medicaid are essential lifelines that millions of Americans rely on, and I absolutely oppose any efforts to cut funding or impose restrictions that would limit care.</b>&nbsp;</p> <p>While Donald Trump and Congressional Republicans try to take these benefits away, I am committed to ensuring that you receive the benefits and care you need, deserve, and is rightfully yours.&nbsp;</p> <p>As someone who grew up without health insurance and whose family nearly went bankrupt due to pneumonia I had as a kid, I understand firsthand why healthcare should be a right, not a privilege. That is why I am a founding member of the Medicare for All Caucus, leading the fight to ensure no one is forced to delay care or suffer because they cannot afford treatment. I also strongly support the Medicare for All Act, which creates a single-payer system that guarantees healthcare for all, regardless of income or employment status, while eliminating copays and premiums.&nbsp;</p> <p>In addition to defending these programs, I’ve introduced legislation to strengthen and expand access to social security and healthcare:&nbsp;</p> <ul style="list-style-type: disc;"> <li>The <b>Social Security 2100 Act</b>: Increases benefits, improves the Cost-of-Living Adjustment (COLA), so it reflects the inflation experienced by seniors; and ensure no one retires into poverty after a full career of work by improving benefits for long-serving, low-wage workers.&nbsp;</li> </ul> <ul style="list-style-type: disc;"> <li>The <b>Choose Medicare Act</b>: Expands Medicare by creating Medicare Part E, available to every individ

Women | U.S. Representative Jimmy Gomez The 2022 Supreme Court decision to overturn Roe v. Wade dismantled almost 50 years of precedent that affirmed the constitutional right of every woman to make decisions about her body, health, and future. This ruling put the lives and freedoms of millions of Americans at risk---especially people of color, low-income families, LGBTQ+ individuals, and survivors of abuse. I was outraged, and I knew we had to fight back.</p> <p>Since then, I’ve worked with my colleagues in Congress to restore and protect reproductive rights, expand access to healthcare, and stand up for women and families across the country. </p> <p><b>Reproductive Rights</b></p> <p>I co-sponsored the <b>Ensuring Women’s Right to Reproductive Freedom Act (H.R. 782)</b>, which protects the right to travel across state lines for abortion care, and the <b>Right to Contraception Act (H.R. 999)</b> to guarantee access to contraceptives and protect healthcare providers’ ability to offer related services and information.</p> <p>In the 119<sup>th</sup> Congress, I’ve continued this work by supporting critical legislation that addresses access, privacy, and the right to choose. I am a proud supporter of the <b>Women’s Health Protection Act of 2025 (H.R. 12)</b> to defend the right to abortion care at the federal level and the <b>Access to Birth Control Act (H.R. 4084)</b> to ensure pharmacies provide timely, unobstructed access to contraception. I also co-sponsored the <b>My Body, My Data Act (H.R. 3916)</b> to protect sensitive reproductive health information from surveillance or misuse, and the <b>Menstrual Equity for All Act (H.R. 364)</b> to make menstrual products more accessible in schools, shelters, and public spaces. </p> <p><b>Civil Rights</b></p> <p>In addition, I support the <b>Equality Act (H.R. 15)</b> to ban discrimination based on sex, sexual orientation, and gender identity, and the <b>Respect for Marriage Act</b>, which safeguards marriage equality for same-sex and interracial couples.</p> <p>I remain committed to defending the rights of all peopl

Healthcare | U.S. Representative Jimmy Gomez <p>I grew up without health insurance, so I know how hard it can be to get the care you need. That’s why I believe healthcare is a right, not a privilege, and why I’m committed to making sure everyone, no matter their background or income, can access quality, affordable healthcare. <strong></strong></p> <p><strong>Medicare for All</strong></p> <p>I am proud to have authored the <b>Chose Medicare Act (H.R. 3911)</b>, which would create a Part E public health plan, giving people more affordable healthcare insurance options --- especially those who don’t qualify for traditional Medicare or Medicaid, or who find private insurance too expensive. It would help lower costs, reduce paperwork, and increase competition in the insurance market, so more families can get the care they need without worrying about high premiums or surprise medical bills. I co-sponsored <b>the Medicare for All Act (H.R. 3514)</b> to establish a national, improved Medicare-for-All program that guarantees healthcare as a right for all Americans. I also support the <b>Health Care Affordability Act of 2025 (H.R. 247)</b>. This bill expands eligibility for the refundable credit for coverage under a qualified health plan, making healthcare more accessible. </p> <p><b>Women’s Health</b></p> <p>I believe in protecting every person’s right to make their own decisions about pregnancy. Abortion is healthcare. That’s why I support the <b>Women’s Health Protection Act of 2025 (H.R.12)</b>, which safeguards an individual’s ability to choose whether to continue or end a pregnancy without interference. This bill also ensures that healthcare providers can offer abortion services without fear of legal or political retaliation. Protecting reproductive freedom is essential to health and autonomy. The <b>My Body, My Data Act of 2025 (H.R. 3916),</b> which I am a sponsor of, aims to protect the privacy of personal reproductive and sexual health information. Energy and Environment | U.S. Representative Jimmy Gomez <strong><span style="font-size: 16px;"></span></strong> <p>We are at a critical moment for our environment and public health. Climate change and environment injustice are already affecting communities across the country---especially low-income neighborhoods and communities of color. As a father, I know we need to take action now, to ensure that we can leave a legacy behind that we are proud of. That’s why I am committed to advancing legislation that protects public lands, expands access to reliable infrastructure, and defends the well-being on animals and people alike. </p> <p><b>Conservation</b></p> <p>I’m proud to support the <b>Rim of the Valley Corridor Preservation Act (H.R. 3874)</b>, which expands the Santa Monica Mountains National Recreation Area by more than 191,000 acres. This bill ensures that future generations will be able to enjoy the unique beauty of Southern California’s natural landscapes—while also protecting wildlife habitats and green spaces from overdevelopment.</p> <p><b>Transportation </b></p> <p>Public transportation is a lifeline for millions, yet far too many communities still lack access to reliable, frequent service. That’s why I co-sponsored the <b>Stronger Communities through Better Transit Act (H.R. 3449)</b>, which provides direct federal operating support for local transit agencies. This funding helps improve service, reduce wait times, and connect more people, especially in underserved neighborhoods, to jobs, schools, and essential services, while taking cars off the streets to protect our environment. </p> <p><b>Water</b></p> <p>Access to clean, affordable water is a basic human right—not a luxury. That’s why I am a co-sponsor of the <b>Water Affordability, Transparency, Equity, and Reliability (WATER) Act of 2025 (H.R. 3376)</b> which establishes a permanent federal trust fund to upgrade our nation’s crumbling water and sewer infrastructure. Education | U.S. Representative Jimmy Gomez I went through public schools, started at community college, and made my way to UCLA. Like so many students, I walked out with a degree and a stack of student loans. That debt followed me into the start of my career and shaped choices I had to make about work, family, and my future. I know firsthand how heavy that burden feels when you’re just trying to get your life moving.</p> <p>That’s why I fight to make sure students can pursue higher education without being crushed by debt. I’ve already turned that experience into action—passing a law to make years of student loan forgiveness tax free, and introducing legislation to make that relief permanent.
